vectors.rule: Only the lines between on and off are Markdown
Text sent while Markdown is off is shown as sent
BEL ends a sequence as ST does
An on sequence in the middle of a line takes effect from the next line
Text after an off sequence on a Markdown line is still part of that Markdown line
An on sequence while Markdown is on starts a new message
A new message ends a code block left open in the one before
A parameter with an unknown name is ignored, and the others still count
A sequence with an unknown first field is ignored
A prompt ended by Go Ahead is shown as sent, and Markdown stays on after it
A prompt ended by End of Record is shown as sent
An off sequence while Markdown is off does nothing
An off sequence ends an open code block, which the next message does not reopen
An off sequence ends a table, and a row in the next message does not rejoin it
An off sequence closes an open section, and the next message starts outside it
An off sequence ends a list, so an indented line in the next message is a paragraph
A sequence with no terminator by the end of its line is abandoned and none of it is shown
A row waiting for its delimiter row when a prompt arrives is a paragraph
A prompt ends a table
A row still waiting for its delimiter row when the message ends is a paragraph
After an on sequence in the middle of a Markdown line, the rest of the line stays in the old message
An SGR sequence before an on sequence does not put it in the middle of the line
A sequence of 256 bytes, from its ESC through its terminator, is read
Every newline is a line break
An empty line is a blank line
Leading spaces on a paragraph are dropped
Four leading spaces do not make a code block
Trailing spaces are dropped
A leading tab counts as four spaces
A tab serves as the space after a marker
A carriage return before the newline is not part of the line
A line of spaces only is a blank line
## and a space make a level 2 heading
One to six # give levels 1 to 6
Seven # start a paragraph
A # with no space after it starts a paragraph
A closing run of # is dropped
A # alone on a line is an empty heading
A heading whose closing run leaves no text is empty
A heading may follow a paragraph with no blank line
A heading's text holds inline markup
A heading may sit in a block quote
Text followed by a line of dashes is a paragraph and a rule
Text followed by a line of equals signs is two paragraphs
One star on each side makes italic
One underscore on each side makes italic
Two stars on each side make bold
Two underscores on each side make bold
Three stars on each side make bold italic
Two tildes on each side strike text through
A single tilde is shown as typed
Bold nests inside italic
Stars inside a word make italic
Strikethrough and bold combine
Bold, italic and strikethrough combine
Italic nests inside bold
Two underscores make bold, so with a star inside they make bold italic and no underline
A code span may sit in bold
A marker never closed on its line is shown as typed
Emphasis does not reach across a newline
A backslash before a star shows the star
Underscores inside a word are shown as typed
A star with spaces on both sides is shown as typed
Backticks make a code span
Two backticks open a span that can hold one
One space is dropped from each end of a code span
Markdown is not read inside a code span
A backtick never closed on its line is shown as typed
Three backticks open and close a code block, and its lines are shown as sent
Three tildes open and close a code block
A closing line longer than the opening one closes the block
A line shorter than the opening one is code
Text after the opening characters is the language
Markdown is not read inside a code block
An empty line inside a code block is a line of code
A code block left open ends with its message
The opening line's indentation is dropped from each line of code
A closing line may be indented and end in spaces
A line with text after the closing characters is code
An opening line of backticks with a backtick later on it is a paragraph
A code block is not recognized inside a block quote
A code block indented under a list item ends the list and is not nested
A dash, a star or a plus marks a bulleted item
A number and a dot mark a numbered item
A number and a closing parenthesis mark a numbered item
The number of an item is shown as sent
An item indented to the text of the item above is nested in it
input:
]67;1\- Weapons
  - a rusty sword
  - a bow
- Armor
]67;0\

vectors.rule: Lists nest to a third level
A numbered list nests in a bulleted item
An indented line that is not an item continues the item above
[ ] and [x] after the marker make a task
input:
]67;1\- [ ] find the key
- [x] open the gate
]67;0\

vectors.rule: An item's text holds inline markup
Indentation before the first item of a list does not nest it
A blank line does not end a list
A bulleted list may follow a paragraph with no blank line
A numbered item may follow a paragraph with no blank line, whatever its number
A line that is not indented does not join the item above it
A marker with no text after it is a paragraph
A marker with no space after it is a paragraph
A heading is not read inside an item
A line that starts with a star and a space is a list item, so a server escapes the star of an emote
A task's box is part of the item's text, so a child indented two spaces nests under it
A task's box may follow a number
An item indented less than the text of every open item is at the first level
A line of text indented to an outer item's text closes the nested item and continues the outer one
A heading indented under an item is a heading, and ends the list
A second list marker at the start of an item's text is text
A quoted line ends a list outside the quote
An upper-case X marks a task done
A box with no text after it is the item's text
A > puts the line in a block quote
The space after > is optional
Each further > adds a level, with or without spaces between
A list may sit in a block quote
Spaces after the quote marker's own space indent what follows, so lists nest inside a quote
A > with nothing after it is a blank line in the quote
A quote may follow a paragraph with no blank line
A line with no > is not in the quote
Three dashes make a rule
Three stars make a rule
Three underscores make a rule
Spaces between the characters are allowed
A long row of dashes is a rule
Two dashes are a paragraph
Mixed characters are a paragraph
A row of equals signs is a paragraph
A rule may sit in a block quote
A header row, a delimiter row and rows make a table
Colons in the delimiter row set each column's alignment
The | at the end of a row is optional
A table may have no rows under its header
A cell holds inline markup
\| puts a | in a cell, also inside a code span
A row with too few cells gets empty ones
Cells beyond the header's count are dropped
Rows with no delimiter row after the first are paragraphs
A delimiter row with a different number of cells makes no table
A row followed by another row is a paragraph, and the second row is tried as a header
A blank line ends a table
A line that does not start with | ends a table
Rows that do not start with | make no table
A table is not recognized inside a block quote
A | in the middle of a line makes no table
[text](destination) is a link
A title in double quotes follows the destination
A title may be in single quotes
A destination between < and > may hold spaces
A percent-encoded destination is kept as written
A link's text holds emphasis
A web address between < and > is a link to itself
A mailto: address between < and > is a link to itself
A bare web address is a link, without the punctuation that ends it
A closing parenthesis with no opening one in the address is not part of it
Punctuation is taken off the end of a bare address one character at a time
A title in parentheses is not read, and the link is shown as typed
A destination with a percent-encoded configuration is kept as written
A local: destination with a title is a note with a tooltip
input:
]67;1\[the iron door](local: "It needs a silver key")
]67;0\

vectors.rule: A destination with no scheme is parsed as written, and the OSC 8 standard gives it no action
A link not closed on its line is shown as typed
A backslash before [ stops a link
A reference-style link is shown as typed
A link definition is a paragraph
An image is shown as its alt text, linked to the address
A bare www. address is not a link
A mail address between < and > with no mailto: is not a link
Between < and >, only web and mail addresses are links
An HTML tag is shown as typed
An MXP tag is shown as typed
An entity is shown as typed
A backslash at the end of a line is shown
A backslash before a letter is shown
A backslash before a # stops a heading
Angle brackets and ampersands in ordinary text are shown as typed
<details>, a summary line and </details> make a section that starts folded
<details open> makes a section that starts unfolded
A summary holds inline markup
With no summary line the summary is empty
A summary line counts only straight after the opening line
Sections nest, and </details> closes the innermost
A section holds any Markdown lines
Spaces around a section line are allowed
<details> with other text on its line is a paragraph
</details> with no section open is a paragraph
A summary line with no opening line before it is a paragraph
A section is not recognized inside a block quote
A color sequence before a marker does not hide the marker
A sequence between the two stars of a marker does not split it
A sequence before a # does not stop the heading
Markdown bold leaves the color as it was
A 24-bit color works on a Markdown line
Underline comes from SGR and sits beside Markdown styles
SGR underline combines with Markdown bold italic
SGR underline and color combine with Markdown bold
Color works inside a code span
Color works inside a code block, and colored tildes do not close a backtick block
An OSC 8 link works on a Markdown line
An OSC 8 link left open carries across lines until its own sequence ends it
Where an OSC 8 link covers part of a Markdown link's text, no Markdown link is made
A color left on carries into the Markdown lines that follow
A color left on carries past the end of the message
Each named value marks its message
Six hexadecimal digits mark a message with a color
An unknown value is no mark
none is no mark
Parameters come in any order
When a name appears twice, the last one counts
A change sequence sets the mark of the message its id names, also while Markdown is off
A change sequence leaves Markdown on
A change for an unknown id is ignored
A change to an unknown value is ignored
A change with no mark is ignored
A change with no id is ignored
An id with a character outside its set is ignored, and the other parameters still count
A change to none removes the mark
An id names the most recent message that used it
